_about: H1 The kicking knee (and the cast). docs/archive/clinic/clinic-design-v1.md Q4 H1 and the quality pass Q1-Q7; contract docs/architecture/clinic-heal-api.md. Levels are data: each row's decider (a count, a side, a path order) is drawn from the level's lists. Words: real Kutchi only from data/cook.json (same ids); everything else is an English placeholder ({"placeholder": true}), shown as [EN: ...] until the family gives the word. Level 1 carries two real-Kutchi counts so a blind bot stays under 10% (build/leak_clinic_heal_a.mjs).

camera._about: D2 (1 Oct): the wide shot the zoom starts from, chosen by the angle the close-up needs (front-on or side-on). No side-on sitting pose exists yet: 'side' uses the front pose until the art batch (art list A1).
camera._target: A1 (5 Oct): the match cut. target = where the close-up draws the sore part and size = its radius, in the close-up's 800 x 500 units: the push-in ends with the patient's part (from the art's anchor) at that place and size.

art._about: heal-A, 2 Oct: the close-up art swaps in by file name (docs/design-language/art-plans/clinic-heal-art-plan.md § 8). The code draws the stand-in until `on` is true; the cut session sets `on` once the file exists. box = where the picture sits, in the close-up's svg units (800 x 500).

knee._a1: A1 (5 Oct): K1 placed so its knee joint (730, 360 in the 1536 x 1024 source) sits on the game's knee (440, 250) at 0.66 (the knee about half the height, art plan 3.2); scale = how much bigger than the stand-in the knee is drawn (the dots, the wrap and the hammer follow it); split = the svg y where the shin starts (the kick swings K1's own shin until K2 is cut).

wrap._about: CLN-100 (9 Oct): the wrap's anchors on K1's outline, in the source picture's pixels (src). back = the thigh's underside, the crease, the shin's back (top to bottom); front = above the kneecap, the kneecap, below it. Every turn runs from one to the other and is masked to the leg; skin = the skin's left edge (the trouser cuff and its shadow are never wrapped over), top to bottom; band = the bandage's width.
